Title: Intro to Bead Crochet
Description: Students will learn the basics of crocheting with beads as well as the basics of how to create their own simple bead crochet patterns. By the end of this class, students will have completed a small bead crochet project.
Student Provides: Size 10 crochet thread, 1.25 mm crochet hook, size 6/0 beads in 4 different colors (at least 150 of each color), sewing needle (with eye large enough to thread crochet thread and SMALL enough fit through your beads), and scissors

Title: Glove Making by Hand
Description: Students will learn how to measure for a pattern, cut, and sew gloves by hand. Students must be skilled with accurate cutting and even hand stitching.
Kit Contents: Fabric for one pair of gloves, matching thread, needles, frix-on pen, pattern, instructions
Student Provides: Small sharp scissors, pins

Title: No Stone Unturned: An Introduction to Rhinestoning
Description: Learn how to make rhinestone designs on fabric using Preciosa stones and E-6000 glue. Students will make samples for future reference and bring home a design of their own creation.
Kit Contents: Two colors of Preciosa rhinestones in five sizes, two colors of practice rhinestones, one kneaded eraser, two trays, a stylus, syringes, one tube of e-6000 glue, one mask
Student Provides: OPTIONAL: preferred mask type for use with glue, accessories or clothing to decorate (ex. shoes, purses, headbands, T-shirts, and jewelry), design stencils

Title: Draping a Basics Bodice on a Corseted Figure
Description: Using professional modern fashion industry techniques, Lana Lily will walk students through the process of draping a single dart Basic Bodice on a fellow corseted student model. The techniques used here can be transferred to most time periods and this basic bodice shape can be used to pattern any bodice for this corseted shape.
Student Provides: Cotton twill fabric, 2” safety pins, sharp fabric scissors, straight pins, narrow elastic, ball point pen or pencil for markings, fitted ¾ or long sleeve crew neck shirt, and corset that student wishes to be draped in

Title: Intro to Fingerloop Weaving
Description: Discover the ancient art of fingerloop braiding in this beginner-friendly class. Learn to create decorative cords using loop manipulation techniques from medieval Europe. This craft was used for centuries to accent clothing and make functional cords.
Kit Contents: 3 skeins of silk embroidery floss and one binder clip
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Draping a Basics Bodice on a Corseted Figure
Description: Using professional modern fashion industry techniques, Lana Lily will walk students through the process of draping a single dart Basic Bodice on a fellow corseted student model. The techniques used here can be transferred to most time periods and this basic bodice shape can be used to pattern any bodice for this corseted shape. Please note students should be comfortable with another student using them as a live model for this process which can take up to 2 hours of standing.
Student Provides: Cotton twill fabric, 2” safety pins, sharp fabric scissors, straight pins, narrow elastic, ball point pen or pencil for markings, fitted ¾ or long sleeve crew neck shirt, and corset that student wishes to be draped in

Title: Intro to Fingerloop Weaving
Description: Discover the ancient art of fingerloop braiding in this beginner-friendly class. Learn to create decorative cords using loop manipulation techniques from medieval Europe. This craft was used for centuries to accent clothing and make functional cords. Master foundational techniques like loop formation, basic patterns, and historical applications.
Kit Contents: 3 skeins of silk embroidery floss and one binder clip
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Introduction to Pattern Drafting
Description: We will be learning how to apply the three principles of pattern making: dart manipulation, added fullness, and contouring, to a basic block pattern in order to create your own patterns! These techniques can be applied whether you’re making your own patterns from scratch or looking to adapt or fix existing patterns.
Kit Contents: Scaled pattern blocks for practice, clear grid ruler, French curve ruler
Student Provides: Scissors, scotch tape, pencil

Title: First Bustle Era Placemat Hat Workshop
Description: The return of the placemat millinery class! This year’s version is a beginner-friendly 1870s first/early bustle era placemat hat! Come learn how to make a Victorian 'perching hat'! Equally perfect for simple looks or as a grand statement piece, the percher hat hits near the front of your hairline and rests on the mid-scalp, then comes up off the back in either a curve or a turn up.
Kit Contents: Instructions including photos for both hat styles, placemat, heavy duty needle, thread, shaping wire, fabric lengths for ruffling, and ribbon trims
Student Provides: Scissors, seam ripper, measuring tape, and any extra trim they want to add

Title: Piped Prairie Point Trim
Description: Prairie points are a traditional quilting trim, but they can also be applied to evening fabrics for a chic and exotic touch. Come learn how to construct this trim from bias fabric from guest teacher, Kenneth D. King.
Kit Contents: Handouts
Student Provides: Sewing machine, ½ yd crisp fabric (shirting cotton or taffeta), ½ yd white paper, basic sewing kit (needles, thread, scissors), rotary blade and cutting mat. OPTIONAL: 1/4 inch adjustable zipper foot

Title: Creating Felted Applique for Clothing
Description: If you would like to replicate the floral designs on a 1920s cloche hat, augment a pocket, lapel, or unmentionable border with a lovely design, or go wild on a cape or cosplay creation, this class is for you. All materials will be supplied to make a lovely tuna can incursion. From there the world will be your oyster or huckleberry or whatever your muse desires.
Kit Contents: Tuna can, felt, batting, glue, embroidery floss, specialty needles, freezer paper and handout
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit, scissors, any decorative beads you want to use, transfer pencil, chalk or pen, and tape measure

Title: Intermediate Ribbon Millinery Flowers - Level 1
Description: Take your ribbon flower skills to the next level! You will begin to learn how to shape and sculpt flat ribbons to create beautiful and exquisite flowers. We will discuss how milliners in the past used math and proportion combined with their artistry to create the decorations we so admire today. Students must have basic hand sewing skills.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut and pre-sealed synthetic ribbon lengths, threads, needles, beads and detailed, and handouts
Student Provides: Embroidery scissors and beeswax. OPTIONAL: vision aids like eyeglasses or magnification

Title: The Amazing Diversity of Victorian Jewelry
Description: Since antiquity, women have decked themselves with hand-crafted jewelry, but the 19th Century Industrial Revolution enabled quality pieces to become available to all. This lecture presents an overview of Victorian jewelry art, from swoon-inducing pieces worn by royalty and dollar princesses to affordable ones created for middle class wives and daughters, as well as ones from your teacher’s personal collection. You’ll be astonished by the variety of materials used to create genuine beauty in these humble, as well as spectacular, female adornments.

Title: Cosplay: Accuracy vs. Interpretation
Description: The joy of Cosplay is in representing your character well. Nancy and Lorelei Howe will discuss whether character accuracy or creativity in interpretation is most important, and other related topics.

Title: Fashioning Identity: Is This Dress Me
Description: Clothes have meaning. A leather jacket means something different than a blazer. In this class, we will explore how we are constantly using the complex language of fashion to say something about ourselves to the people around us.

Title: Creating Narrative Illustrations in Costumes
Description: This lecture will look at how costumes can be used as art pieces to tell a narrative or capture moments in time from a piece of film. We will look at how you can use embellishments to show character, show scenes from film, and create easter eggs. Among other examples we will look at a narrative piece made representing Howl Pendragon from Howl’s Moving Castle, which represents the character but, through beadwork, revealing layers, and embroidery, also represents facets of the main character’s journey. These couture reveals create intrigue in costumes as art pieces.

Title: Fitting and Adjusting a Victorian Bodice Pattern
Description: We will demonstrate the process of fitting a Victorian Bodice, using our expertise in theatrical and historical contexts. We will then demonstrate transferring the fitting changes to the paper pattern.

Title: Journey Through Arthurian Costume
Description: We’ll examine the evidence for a historical Arthur, then compare and contrast that with portrayals of his court across popular media. How did we get from a 5th Century Romanized Briton war leader to the epitome of chivalrous nobility, anyway? And exactly how long would it really take an Arthurian knight to dress out in his worthiest armor? Hopefully you’ll leave with a few fun and/or interesting new facts with which to amaze your friends at your next round-table discussion.

Title: Sleeve Anatomy and How to Tweak It
Description: This class will cover the “anatomy” of a sleeve and how to modify a flat-patterned sleeve to dramatically alter the look of your costume. We’ll go over different styles of sleeves that can be used to achieve certain effects and tips about armhole-to-sleeve relationships will also be addressed.

Title: Spandex Doesn’t Scare Me
Description: Many people who sew are afraid of moving from woven fabrics to stretch, but I can show you why you shouldn’t be scared to use spandex (aka Lycra) to get the effects you’re after, easily! I’ve been sewing as a dance mum for many years (and making my own leotards for ballet class when they were only available in black, black, or black in my size) and I’ve used this as a basis for many of my cosplays over the years since 1985. You’ll see examples of what fabrics to use, what stitches to use or not use, and learn whether you need an overlocker/serger to get the best results.

Title: Basic Leatherworking: Creating a Bracer
Description: In this workshop, students will create a single leather bracer custom fit to them by first creating a paper pattern to their measurements, tooling a simple stamped design, dying the leather, setting grommets, and finishing.
Kit Contents: Piece of 8 oz leather, leather dye, dauber, exacto knife, groove cutter, grommets, use of setting tools and presses, lacing cord, and beveler
Student Provides: Paper, pencil, and measuring tape

Title: Great Shots: Costume Photography with your Phone
Description: This class will teach students how to take great costume shots using their smartphones. We will address coaching others how to pose, finding good lighting, shooting from good angles, and much more, in order to produce the most flattering shot for you and your subject. We will also address how to take great costume pictures of yourself, when you have no one around to assist you. As part of the class, we will be leaving the classroom and visiting various places around the hotel to practice taking pictures.
Kit Contents: Handout containing tips, tricks, editing app recommendations, and equipment recommendations
Student Provides: A smartphone, preferably from the last few years with available memory and battery. Be prepared to be photographed (dressing up is encouraged), and to be outside for a short time. OPTIONAL, but recommended: a tripod with a smartphone attachment and remote shutter

Title: A Touch of Elegance: Regency Fashion Accessories
Description: Accessories are important for getting one in the right mood and into character to help achieve that wonderful and elusive feeling of stepping back in time. The accessories you carry or wear will help convey who you are when you wave your fan, adjust your cravat, or saunter with your cane. This talk will include an overview of men and ladies Regency accessories using digital images and actual examples of reticules, hats, fans, fobs, parasols etc.

Title: Historically Informed Modern Etiquette
Description: Whether hosting a historically adequate tea party or engaging in standard conversation, good etiquette will make your life more enjoyable. Learn some of the history of etiquette and how to apply it to modern life. This class will discuss everything from how to introduce people to proper place settings for a dinner party.

Title: How to NOT to Look Awkward in Photos
Description: Hate having your picture taken? Let’s fix that! Do you panic when someone pulls out a camera? Awkward hands? Stiff smile? That “OMG what do I do with my face” moment? You’re not alone. Good news: Looking great in photos isn’t about being photogenic, it’s about knowing a few simple tricks and I’m about to teach you how to stop looking like a deer in headlights and start looking like you actually know what you’re doing. You’ll learn the “Turtle Neck” Trick, how to “Smize,” the “Turn Slightly” Rule, what to do with your hands, how to look natural, not like a stiff robot, and more. By the end, you’ll go from “OMG delete that” to “Damn, I look good!”

Title: Unusual Materials and Effects
Description: How to use items not usually considered in costuming with spectacular results, including cellophane wrap, angellina fiber, hot glue, and foam for fabrics, faux raised work, and digigrade body shaping.

Title: Kimono: A Cultural History
Description: Sometimes there is a misconception that traditional or non-Western dress is something that is fixed and unchanging. This course will explore how the Japanese kimono has evolved through the centuries, just as European fashion has, and continues to evolve today.

Title: Are You Crochet Curious
Description: This class is for those who would like to try crocheting for the first time. We will cover the basic foundations of crochet: chain stitch, single crochet, double crochet, changing yarn, and finishing off your project. We will start working on a scarf and I’ll help you make a plan for more accessories for costumes.
Kit Contents: Pouch with stitch markers, sewing needle
Student Provides: 6.5 ergonomic crochet hook, medium weight Red Heart skein in any pastel color (not white)

Title: Filled Tubing and its Application
Description: In this class, you’ll learn how to use bias-fabric tubing to make an amazing braided trim. If you can do a basic crocheted chainstitch, you can make this rich-looking trim from a length of bias tubing which can be applied as an amazing accent on any outfit.
Kit Contents: Handouts
Student Provides: Sewing machine, 3/4 yd crisp fabric (taffeta, dupioni, or shirting cotton), 3 yd 3 mm thick rattail or ¼” thick “shoelace” cord, square of ground fabric backed with wool flannel or craft felt, crochet hook, ½ yd white paper, basic sewing kit (needles, thread, scissors), rotary blade and cutting mat. OPTIONAL: 1/4 inch adjustable zipper foot

Title: Coloring Ribbon
Description: Buying manufactured wired ombre and variegated ribbon has become more and more expensive. Coloring light colored ribbon is one way to reduce this cost. This class will have hands-on practice with different methods of coloring ribbon to create ombre, variegated and other effects on different types of white ribbon. The dried ribbons can be attached to a sample page with notes. The pages can be inserted into a binder for a sample book at home.
Kit Contents: Disposable plastic apron, disposable nitrile gloves, ribbons, paint brushes, paint pallet, sample documentation sheets, coloring supplies, liquid droppers
Student Provides: 2-3 14 oz sealable glass jars, heat gun or hair dryer, 1 full newspaper, pen or pencil, small misting spray bottle. OPTIONAL: water repellent apron and gloves

Title: Burn it: Fabric 101 and Identification
Description: Weaves, substrates, oh my! Did you pick up a fabric at Bargain Basement and you’re not sure what kind of lining to use? Do you suspect that the “rayon satin” is actually polyester satin in the Fabric District, but you’re not sure if you’re being ripped off? In this class, we will talk about the basics of textiles and how to identify mystery fabrics to ensure the success of your project. We’ll cover the basics of how fabric works, what it’s made of, and how to tell what you’ve got when there’s no label. There will be swatches to feel and demonstrations of the burn test.

Title: Color Me Impressed: Next Level Color Theory
Description: Interested in learning more about color than was taught in your primary school art class? Know the basics, but looking for more technical knowledge? Lorelei will be teach you all about complementary colors, the different color wheels, how to make pleasing color combinations, how to use color in character design, and more.

Title: Roll-Pinning for a Smooth Bodice
Description: Roll-pinning is a theatrical method of flatlining a bodice to account for the curve around the body, to ensure a smoother finish. We will demonstrate the technique on both a princess line and a darted bodice and a fitted sleeve.

Title: The Ins and Outs Of Entering A Costume Competition
Description: Are you interested in entering a costume competition? Don’t know where to start? Join Paige and Elee in answering all your ‘Where to begin’ questions. We will be covering from how to enter to what’s next. Join us for an hour of questions and answers, build books, and so much more.

Title: Mapping Out Your Costume Adventure
Description: Do you find yourself sewing in the car on the way to events? Do you have trouble figuring out where to start on a project? In this interactive class, we will discuss ways to plan out a costume project so you can finish on time, under budget, with a result you can be proud of. Using ideas from business project management, paired with theater design techniques, and costumed event experience, you can learn how to set and meet your costuming goals.

Title: Button, Button, Who’s Got the Button
Description: Needle-lace buttons used on clothing were fashioned by hand from about 1650 to 1900. Students will learn the basic technique and create various samples of Dorset buttons created with various sizes of rings and threads.
Kit Contents: Rings, threads, needles, and handout
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Hair Flower Whimsy
Description: Making fun hair accessories of faux flowers and shiny bits to add flair and color to hairstyles for any day or occasion.
Kit Contents: Hair clips, silk flowers, brads, shiny bits and bobs as possible bling
Student Provides: Glue gun and glue sticks, special embellishments such as feathers, gems, glitter glue, or fun buttons/small toy pieces

Title: This Girl is on Fire: Leather Burning
Description: Add to your leather craft skills and learn how to burn into leather. Students will complete their pyrography designs on a leather cuff, learning techniques that can be used on other surfaces as well.
Kit Contents: Walnut Hollow Wood Burning Tool, fiberglass mat, scrap leather, 1.5 inch leather cuff
Student Provides: Pliers

Title: Viking/Fantasy Leather War Belt
Description: In this class, students will learn the basics of leather carving and finishing as they decorate a wide, segmented “war belt”. This belt will greatly enhance your fantasy, barbarian, or viking costume and can be made to fit any size. This war belt is made with a lot of leather and is 4-5 inches tall with a big plaque in front (think something like a wrestling championship belt, but not quite that huge!).
Kit Contents: Pre-cut leather pieces, straps, buckles and rivets, decorative carving pattern options, 3 decorative metal mountings, and water based paints and dyes
Student Provides: Apron, gloves, acrylic paint (if student wants a specific color), paint brushes, pencil or pen, paper/craft scissors, leather tools if you have them

Title: DIY Millinery: Making Hats From Your Sewing Stash
Description: Purchasing beautifully made historical and/or costume hats are often an expensive investment. Come hear how you can pattern and create your own hats from your sewing and cosplay making stash, as well as household items. This lecture and demo will help those who would like to dip their toes into making their own hats!

Title: Textiles: Natural Fibers
Description: What makes a fabric? A discussion of natural materials, including what we use them for, what properties make them useful, where they come from, and how we have changed them over the centuries.

Title: Beginning Smocking
Description: Smocking is an embroidery technique performed on pleated fabric and was extremely popular in the Victorian and Edwardian eras. But it actually predates this, going as far back as the Middle Ages. In this class, we’ll cover how to do the pleating (especially if you do not have a pleater) and basic stitches to accomplish designs.
Kit Contents: Pre-smocked fabric, plastic canvas, fabric marker, needle and floss
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit

Title: Intro to Irish Crochet Lace
Description: This class will introduce students to the basics of Irish Crochet lace making. By the end of class, students will have completed their own small piece of lace and will have the foundation to work on larger projects. Students should already know the basics of how to crochet for this class (SC, DC, TC, ST, etc).
Kit Contents: Size 10 crochet thread, handouts with patterns, thread, and a small piece of fabric
Student Provides: 1mm crochet hook, scissors, sewing needle, OPTIONAL: thimble (if you regularly use one), Size 20 or Size 60 crochet thread (if you desire a more delicate lace)

Title: Knitting Up, Down, and in the Round
Description: Join our ‘Knitting Up, Down, and in the Round: Intro to Working with Circular Knitting Needles’ class, perfect for beginners. Learn several must-know skills: casting on, knitting, purling, and binding off in the round. Create an easy knit headband using a popular ribbed stitch pattern. Unleash your creativity and master the art of circular knitting!
Kit Contents: 1 skein of yarn and 1 US size 10 circular knitting needles
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Pata de Cabra
Description: Lace making, Pata de Cabra, is a popular technique in Latin America used in clothing. This lace is made by joining two bias tubes together with thread. It originated from a combination of embroidery and Battenburg lace during colonial times. In this class you will learn the techniques.
Kit Contents: Lace, cord, needle, pattern
Student Provides: Scissors and sewing pins

Title: Using the Cricut for Costume Details & Accessories
Description: Curious about the Cricut machine? This class covers (with touchable examples) how the Cricut can be used to create floral embellishments, precision appliques, perfectly cut craft foam, silkscreens for fabric printing, and more. Whether you already own a Cricut or are considering adding one to your toolkit, this is your chance to dive into the endless possibilities, ask questions, and get inspired.

Title: The Puabi Project: Clothing Bronze Age Mesopotamia
Description: This class presents a reenactment project that created an outfit and jewelry from Bronze-Age (Early Dynastic) Mesopotamia based on the lavish burial goods of Puabi of Ur. This project included raising heritage fiber goats, carding, spinning, weaving, dyeing, pattern making, felting kaunakes/kunakku, and jewelry making. The class also discusses techniques for making inferences from limited information and useful information for recreating other Bronze-Age ensembles (Egyptian, Minoan, etc).

Title: The Revival Trends That Shook the 20th Century
Description: The Egyptian revival of the 1920s, Medieval revival of the 1960s, the 1940s’ shoulder pads came back in the 80s! Fashion is cyclical, and this class will dive into how those trends manifest and the spin they put on it.

Title: Deciphering Vintage Unprinted Patterns
Description: Picture this: you just bought a beautiful vintage 1940s pattern from the Bargain Basement. To your horror, you open the pattern to find only blank pieces of tissue and one measly page of instructions. It can be overwhelming at first to work without the familiar markings and words of modern patterns. In this class, you’ll learn how to actually use these patterns. We’ll talk about preserving or caring for the tissue, mending, translating punches to notches, and more.

Title: Basics of Pattern Grading & Resizing
Description: Ever had the struggle of finding a pattern but it isn’t your size? Many vintage patterns and historical pattern books provide just one size for the pattern, leaving the rest of us totally out of luck! Pattern grading is a system that allows you to resize your patterns to any size, larger or smaller, using just some basic rules and the simple slash-and-spread method. We will cover the grading rules for bodices, sleeves, pants, and skirts. Finally, we will apply what we’ve learned to a bodice pattern block, grading it to your size!
Kit Contents: Construction paper for drafting, take home booklet
Student Provides: Pencil, scotch tape, scissors, 18” ruler

Title: Kanzashi Inspired Folded Fabric Flower Hair Clips
Description: Students will learn the basic skills to manipulate fabric to create the petal and leaf forms for Japanese kanzashi flowers. We will look at an overview of how this art is used in Japanese hair ornaments to make many varieties of flowers. Students will get materials to make one complete kanzashi and materials to try at least three different flower structures.
Kit Contents: Assorted petal fabric squares, craft glue, bobbin of thread, needle, cardboard, small pearls, teardrop pearl bead, jewelry wire sample, 2 hair clips, wet wipe, white chord, felt
Student Provides: Small scissors, tweezers

Title: A Work Bag: Practical and Pretty
Description: A work bag has been a practical necessity throughout the ages. Used to carry trinkets, coins, books, pencil, needlework, and project supplies in one place as needed. Create a beautiful, functional bag from a tea towel complete with a pocket and drawstring closure that would be at home in Jane Austin’s drawing room or your cubbie on the mother ship.
Kit Contents: Embroidery floss, tea towel, cord, embroidery needle, ribbon, contrast fabric for pocket, and designs for personalization with script
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit, pins, and scissors. OPTIONAL: fabric and trim scraps, beads, sequins, feathers, fasteners

Title: Kenneth D King’s Greatest Hits
Description: Join us as Kenneth describes his journey as a couture designer, teacher, and writer.

Title: Wonder Woman Appreciation Hour
Description: From her wide-eyed Nazi-punching emergence into Man’s World in 1941 through a brief stint as an Honorary UN Ambassador to her role as an LGBTQ+ icon and advocate for women’s empowerment, Wonder Woman has been through a lot of costume changes. We’ll take a retrospective tour from her origins through the present day and discuss how her wardrobe and accessories have reflected her character’s changing role in society.

Title: Vintage Hair Sets and Styles (1930s-1960s)
Description: This class will go over some basics for styling hair in midcentury styles (1930s–1960s), as well as reading vintage hair setting patterns and diagrams. We’ll go over some tips and tricks I’ve learned over the years on how to maintain rollers, the key to a good brushout, and suggested tools to help you on your way!

Title: Costuming is Character Design: LARP Costume Design
Description: In this class, we will explore how we can use character design rules and principles to create compelling and cohesive costumes for specific characters, taking into account the use, mobility, and the character progression a LARP (live-action-role-playing) character will go through.

Title: Inspired by Film: High Fantasy Ranger Vambraces
Description: Students in this class will build 1 pair of leather 'Ranger Vambraces' (forearm guards) inspired by the style of vambraces worn by the Rangers of Gondor in the 2nd and 3rd Lord of the Rings films. Students will learn the basics of tooling leather, applying dye/finishes, as they create amazing looking leather armor pieces that will make fantastic additions to a Lord of The Rings collection or fantasy costume.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut leather pieces, decorative carving pattern, and water based paints and dyes
Student Provides: Apron, gloves, hair dryer, acrylic paint (if student wants a specific color), paint brushes, pencil or pen, paper/craft scissors, leather tools if you have them

Title: Basic Card Weaving
Description: This class is an introduction to the basic techniques of card or tablet weaving, a very old method of off-loom weaving. This class will discuss materials and methods of creating patterns for garters, belts, and trim. Students will begin work on a pair of garters.
Kit Contents: Cards, rubber band, shuttle, and handouts
Student Provides: 3” C clamp, three colors of same weight worsted yarn or #5 pearl cotton, scissors, and belt

Title: Drafting a Sleeve That Works for Your Body
Description: The class will start with an overview of the mechanics of sleeves. We will work through a basic one piece sleeve draft that will work for most periods, with a focus on ease of movement and create a mockup to check and correct fit issues.
Kit Contents: Pattern paper for one draft, muslin for one sleeve mockup, pencil, and tape measure
Student Provides: Straight edge/ruler, sewing kit for sewing one seam of your mockup. OPTIONAL, but recommended: a bodice you would like to draft a sleeve for

Title: Feathers from Fabric
Description: Using polyester organza, Kenneth will teach you how to make incredible 'feathers' from fabric.
Kit Contents: Handouts
Student Provides: 1 yd poly organza and an alcohol lamp or other small flame source

Title: Sparkling Shoes
Description: Learn how to completely bedazzle a pair of shoes with Preciosa rhinestones and E-6000 glue!
Kit Contents: Rhinestones (size 16 and 12), eraser, trays, stylus, syringes, E-6000 glue, mask
Student Provides: Shoes (not leather), optional: mask, extra rhinestones for colors/patterns

Title: Simple Yet Satisfying Regency Reticule
Description: The Regency silhouette didn’t allow for pockets, hence the ascendance of the reticule. In this workshop, you will make an easy, yet stylish, reticule that features an embroidered applique which you will attach yourself. Minimum skill required, maximum satisfaction assured.
Kit Contents: Pattern, white silky and colored silky lining fabrics, ribbon drawstrings, choice of pre-embroidered applique, hand-outs
Student Provides: Sewing machine, basic sewing kit, needles, straight pins, and white multi-purpose thread

Title: Brazilian Dimensional Embroidery
Description: Add depth to your embellishments with Brazilian Embroidery. This 3-dimensional technique is great for decorating clothing, purses, and customized covered buttons. Students will learn 5 different stitches and create a small project.
Kit Contents: Threads, printed fabric, needles, and embroidery hoop
Student Provides: Scissors. OPTIONAL: fabric or project to embroider

Title: A Pressing Matter – AM
Description: After sewing a beautiful seam, it will never look perfect unless it is pressed correctly. Learn tricks of the trade to take your sewing from 'loving hand at home' to 'lovely garments to own.' In this class, students will not only learn more than one way to finish seams of all sorts, but receive other insights to create their costume visions.
Kit Contents: Handout

Title: Leather 101
Description: Come learn the basics you’ll need to start working with leather! We’ll cover the range of the material, tanning methods, thicknesses, and grain types, among other topics. We will also cover where to source it, how to care for it, and much more. There will be some finished projects to see, lots of samples to touch, and several tools to try out!

Title: Procreate for Costume Design & Illustration
Description: This class showcases how to use Procreate and its many features in creating an understandable, adaptive, and beautiful costume design illustration.

Title: Visit to the Symington Resource Center: Part 1
Description: We will share photos and information for all the corsets, flossing and embroidery motif options from the Symington Resource Center, from 1850 through the early 1890s, as well as some interesting bras that we were able to handle and examine.

Title: Queer Expression Through Clothing
Description: Our clothing is unquestionably tied to our identities. Let’s talk about expression, dysphoria, signaling, and how costuming has been a source of freedom for people in the queer community throughout time.

Title: Fitting the Altered Bust
Description: Changes in our bustlines might be natural upon aging or might result from surgical intervention for different reasons. This class will discuss how to alter a bodice pattern to fit such changes, with examples of ways to still achieve a fashionable silhouette.

Title: Hairpiece Basics: Late Regency Era Hair
Description: Learn the basics of using hairpieces. Learn how to match your hair color, where to buy, and even how to make your own. In this class, we will demo how to create Late Regency Era hairstyles (1810–1820) using handmade and ready-made hairpieces. Hair color matching available at the end of class.

Title: Prêt á Cosplay
Description: “It’s attention to detail that makes the difference between average and stunning.” – Francis Atterbury. Have you ever wanted to embody your favorite character, but felt like you’d be all dressed up with no place to go? We’ll discuss history, Disneybounding theory, and how to incorporate those techniques into the capsule closet cosplay street wardrobe of your dreams — ready to take you from the office to dinner to the convention floor.

Title: Create a Foundation Pattern with the Haslam System
Description: This lecture/demo will show you how to create what we call a basic block — referred to as a 'foundation dress pattern' in the Haslam system — in your size. This pattern is then used to reproduce their beautifully drafted vintage designs.

Title: Fashion Laws Through History
Description: When one mentions fashion laws or dress codes, one automatically thinks of the sumptuary laws, but those aren’t the only ones out there. Did you know about the law regarding patent leather shoes or which state prohibited the wearing of high heels? Come and find out more about these and other fashion-based laws.

Title: Beetlemania: The History of Beetle Wing Embroidery
Description: A history of beetle wing embroidery, from its origins in Indian and Thai dress to its expansion into European markets. We’ll cover history, modern examples, and a demo of embroidery techniques.

Title: Ethics in Fabric and Fiber Sourcing
Description: At least 20% of the world’s cotton production comes from enslaved Uyghurs in China. Many synthetic fabrics are responsible for microplastics and serious pollution during production. Many vibrant dyes produce toxic byproducts. What should you look for when sourcing materials for a project to avoid these and other issues? How can you support ethical manufacture of costuming supplies (on a budget)? This class wrestles with these questions.

Title: Smocking and Pleatwork Embroidery 101
Description: Students will learn the basic principles behind the time-honored tradition of smocking and pleatwork embroidery and how it was used in medieval and Early Modern Europe. Students will have the opportunity to complete a small sampler to take home.
Kit Contents: Pre-pleated fabric, embroidery needle, embroidery thread, and instructional handout
Student Provides: Small hand sewing kit (scissors or snips)

Title: Costuming for Film: Shogun World and Beyond
Description: Laura Wong, professional costumer, discusses her work in film and television, including her role as kimono specialist on Westworld's 'Shogun World.' Includes Q&A.

Title: The Social Impact of Huge Edwardian Hats
Description: Edwardian ladies’ hats are some of the biggest, most extravagant ever made. The early 20th century style for giant feathers on these hats brought an extreme demand for feathers, and sometimes entire birds to trim them. This lecture covers memes from the time, the Great Hatpin Peril, and the women who helped save the birds — leading to the creation of the first National Wildlife Refuge and the Audubon Society.

Title: Custom Costumer’s Luggage v2.0
Description: Learn how to transform a basic steamer trunk into a checkable, customizable, budget-friendly luggage solution perfect for costumes. The presenter shares how she designed hers to accommodate bulky, oddly shaped costume pieces. Version 2.0 includes updates from real-world testing, new features, and configuration ideas.

Title: New Life from Old Hats
Description: You can work millinery wonders starting with a hat from the thrift store. Come learn how to reblock felts into historic silhouettes, reshape straws into period bonnets, and refresh or replace trimmings.

Title: Using the Haslam System to Create a 1940s Dress
Description: Using the Haslam System foundation dress pattern, this workshop demonstrates how to recreate 1920s–1950s designs, focusing on a 1940s dress. It covers pattern drafting, where to obtain Haslam books, and differences in foundation patterns across the decades.

Title: Visit to the Symington Resource Center: Part 2
Description: This lecture shares photos and research findings from pants, dresses, jackets, and a special vest from the Symington Resource Center collection (1850–1890s), including garments the instructors examined firsthand.

Title: Pressing Matters: PM
Description: After sewing a beautiful seam, it will never look perfect unless it is pressed correctly. Learn tricks of the trade to take your sewing from 'loving hand at home' to 'lovely garments to own.' This session expands on the morning class with different techniques and applications.
Kit Contents: Handout

Title: Get Crafty with Kanzashi
Description: This beginner-friendly workshop aims to teach the basics of designing and making your own kanzashi hairpins.
Kit Contents: Fabric, assorted hairpins, cording, felt, tweezers, buttons, and fun facts card
Student Provides: Hot glue gun and glue sticks, handsewing needle, thread and scissors

Title: A Brief History of Women’s Eyeglasses
Description: While Dorothy Parker quipped that men seldom make passes at girls who wear glasses, there’s evidence that women wore eyeglasses in days of yore, at least in specific circumstances. This lecture explores historical use of eyeglasses and how to get a more accurate look using modern eyewear.

Title: Don’t Dream It, Make It
Description: We do it all day: dream up garments, costumes, and projects we want to tackle. But how do we get that idea onto paper and then make it plausible? Let’s dive in and find out how to take our creative inspiration from idea to reality.

Title: Beginning Ribbon Trims
Description: In this class, you will learn the techniques used in knife and boxed pleat ribbon trims, which can also be produced with strips of fabric. Multiple variations of pleated trims will be produced using satin ribbon. Sources for additional trims and materials will also be discussed.
Kit Contents: Ribbons, silk pins, cardboard for ruler and gauge, handouts
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit, millinery #3 needles, quilting thread, thread scissors, sewing pins, paper and pen for notes and marking ruler. OPTIONAL: magnification device

Title: Learn Padstitching
Description: What is padstitching and where do you use it? This class will go over the different types of padstitching and where it is typically used. We will also practice the technique on a half-size collar.
Kit Contents: Half size jacket front and collar, fashion fabric and interfacing, needle, and thread
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit and small straight edge

Title: Make a Huge Edwardian Hat
Description: Create your own Edwardian picture hat from a costume shop sombrero. We will start with a black faux felt sombrero, and create a wearable base hat with netting poufs, and hat pins. Multiple colors of tulle and a limited variety of wide ribbons will be available. These hats are LARGE at 22" wide and may not fit in a suitcase. Bring your own large-scale ribbons, flowers, and feathers for a custom look.
Kit Contents: Faux Felt Black Sombrero, tulle netting, tailors wax chalk, two 9” hatpins, and assorted wide ribbons for decoration
Student Provides: Basic hand sewing kit, hot glue gun and glue sticks, craft scissors, and additional decoration for their hat

Title: Mermaid Hair With No Care!
Description: Easy ways to create, wear, and store yarn or hair falls to add volume and/or color to hairstyles for both cosplays and daily wear.
Kit Contents: Variety of colors and weights of yarns and other materials, clips, elastics, ribbon, blue tape, cardboard, and caulk/hot glue
Student Provides: Scissors, and glue gun and glue sticks or small silicone caulk. OPTIONAL: any specific colored yarn, ribbon, or other media they wish to incorporate into a hair fall

Title: Whiskey Helps! - Leather Holder for Your Flask
Description: In this class students will receive a flask (yes! we provide the flask, but not the alcohol!) and then while learning a basic leather stitch, you will create a belt sheath for it to go in, belt loop and all. You will dye it and take home a snazzy flask and sheath.
Kit Contents: Flask, leather pieces, dye, and stitching tools

Title: Pin Keep Project
Description: Make a useful and beautiful pin keep (pin cushion/needle case) using your choice of fabrics. You'll assemble the interior with places for pins, needles, and thread, and decorate the outside to your liking. It's both practical and lovely for your sewing space or travel kit.
Kit Contents: Pin pillow, beeswax, one pack of hand needles, one pack of pins, one thimble, one pair of small scissors
Student Provides: OPTIONAL: any special fabric you would like to use for the exterior (14”x5”), lining (14”x5”), and/or pocket (4”x5”)

Title: Japanese Kimono Today
Description: In this course, we will discuss the role that Japanese kimono play in modern society. We’ll go over the types of kimono (formality, gender, seasonality, etc.), when and how they are worn, and how they continue to evolve. The class ends with a live demonstration of casual kimono dressing, including foundation garments to final styling.

Title: Easy Regency Wraps You Can Create
Description: Fashion plates in ladies’ magazines from 1800–1820 show a variety of lightweight wraps for warm weather. Learn to recreate these stylish Regency accessories by modifying period and modern patterns. The instructor will provide diagrams and bring reproduction garments to examine and try on.

Title: Dyslexic Sewing
Description: If you are dyslexic — or think you might be — come learn about the positives it can bring to costume sewing, and how to avoid some common pitfalls. With 30+ years of sewing experience, Lana Lily will share practical tips and encouragement for dyslexic makers.

Title: The Woven World: Fiber to Fabric
Description: Explore how cultures around the world have created woven textiles from plant and animal fibers. This talk includes examples of traditional looms and weaving techniques from Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas, and how these traditions have evolved or been revived in modern times.

Title: Hand Sewn Housewife
Description: Make a hand-stitched, historically inspired 'housewife' — a portable sewing kit used by soldiers and civilians alike. Learn the stitches needed to assemble a small, functional fabric case with pockets and needle flaps. Perfect for reenactors or hand-sewing enthusiasts.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut fabric pieces, embroidery floss, hand sewing needle, button, ribbon
Student Provides: Small scissors, thimble (optional)

Title: Kumihimo Braiding with Beads
Description: Learn how to create beautiful kumihimo braid jewelry with pre-strung seed beads. You’ll learn to choose materials, follow beading patterns, and place beads while braiding a spiral design using a kumihimo disc.
Kit Contents: 1 Kumihimo disc, 8 weighted bobbins, 1 central weight, beads and cords to make about a 7” long beaded braid, and handout with patterns
Student Provides: OPTIONAL: magnifying glasses

Title: Mouse vs Mucha: Floral and Wire Mouse Ears
Description: Learn how to make custom floral wire mouse ears, similar to theme park headbands, using basic craft supplies. After shaping and securing wire, embellish the headband with flowers and fairy lights.
Kit Contents: Plastic headband with wide hair-comb teeth, silver-colored craft wire, connectors, and warm white battery-operated fairy lights
Student Provides: Small wire cutters, needle nose pliers, sharpie, tape measure, hot glue gun (and drip catcher), glue sticks, craft scissors, and silk flowers. OPTIONAL: bow and small embellishments

Title: Intro to Ottoman Turkish Silk and Gold Embroidery
Description: Learn basic Turkish embroidery stitches using silk and metal threads on open weave fabric. Students will complete an 8"x8" cup cover with decorative corner weights.
Kit Contents: Silk thread, metal thread, prepped background linen, 2 needles (1 large eyed embroidery, 1 large chenille needle), decorative bead/weights, and handouts
Student Provides: 2 pairs of thread snippers (1 for metal threads only, 1 for silk and fabric only)

Title: Cut My Cote: Loom Width & Zero Waste Patterns
Description: For most of history, garments were designed to minimize fabric waste. This class explores how loom width influenced historical garment design and reviews modern zero-waste patterns inspired by these techniques.

Title: My Beads Don’t Hang Straight: 1920s for Curvy Women
Description: This class offers practical costuming advice for curvy women who want to achieve the 1920s look, including undergarment choices, garment modifications, and accessories better suited for fuller figures.

Title: How to Make a Muslin (AKA: Mock-up)
Description: Before you cut into your final fabric, it's best to sew a muslin — but should your muslin really be made of muslin fabric? And how much of your garment do you need to include? Learn what steps are essential and what can be skipped.

Title: Basic Ribbon Flowers and How to Combine Them
Description: Learn to make three basic ribbon flowers and how to combine them for realistic, dimensional effects. Materials seem simple, but the results are magical.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut/sealed ribbon for 6 flowers, thread, needles, beads, and handouts
Student Provides: Embroidery scissors, beeswax. OPTIONAL: vision aids or magnifiers

Title: Corset Flossing Sampler
Description: Learn and practice several corset flossing designs using sampler fabric. This hands-on workshop will teach key decorative and functional stitching techniques.
Kit Contents: Sampler fabric with channels, boning, thread, needle, and handouts
Student Provides: Thimble, thread snips

Title: Let’s Get Knotty: Intro to Tatting
Description: Explore the beautiful art of tatting. Learn foundational stitches and joins using large multicolor thread, then make a butterfly with finer thread.
Kit Contents: 2 bobbin shuttles, picot guide, thread bundles, pouch
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Intermediate Ribbon Trims
Description: Learn four ribbon trim techniques used in the Victorian and Edwardian eras: smocking, quilling, ruching, and twisting (no pleating).
Kit Contents: Ribbons, cardboard ruler, silk pins, handouts
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit, 3 colors of pens, disappearing ink pen. OPTIONAL: magnifier

Title: Rick Rack Rave
Description: Learn to combine crochet stitches with various sizes of rick rack to create stunning lace. You’ll complete both edge and insertion samples.
Kit Contents: Rick rack, crochet thread, hooks, and handouts
Student Provides: Scissors

Title: Cool Tricks with Kenneth D. King
Description: Kenneth will demonstrate and help students construct samples of his favorite couture sewing techniques. Tips, tricks, and professional shortcuts included.

Title: 1928 Seams So Different
Description: Explore key sewing techniques from 1928 manuals vs. modern sewing methods. Topics include seam types, joining shapes, darts, and bust shaping.

Title: Loving Your Reflection
Description: An open conversation about body positivity and the difficult aspects of the clothing industry. How can we harness the power of costume to help ourselves feel more confident, and how can we fight back against a world that profits from low self-esteem?

Title: 1928 Seams So Different
Description: Sewing techniques change over time. We will compare some key sewing techniques from 1928 sewing manuals as taught by the Woman’s Institute of Domestic Arts & Science, London, versus modern sewing techniques. This lecture class will discuss plain seams, overlapped seams, joining shaped edges, dart placement, and sheering for bust fullness.

Title: A History of “Standard” Garment Sizing
Description: Before ready-to-wear, clothing garments were made or modified to fit specific individuals, but mass construction and marketing required standardization into a reasonable number of sizes. How did early manufacturers determine what measurements to use and where did they find them? How standardized are size ranges? How do garment makers determine fit? And what about vanity sizing?

Title: One Skirt, 15 Styles and Counting
Description: Only have enough amazing fabric to make one skirt, but want two or more? Short on closet or suitcase space? Learn how to quickly alter and style a basic full skirt that can be used in multiple costumes.

Title: Shopping in Belle Epoque Paris
Description: We’ll cover the Parisian shopping opportunities for both French women and tourists, middle and upper class. We’ll explore dressmakers, couturiers, and other shopping opportunities. To finish, we’ll examine a first-person account of an American woman shopping for her Parisian trousseau in 1875.

Title: Fabric Manipulation for Eco-Friendly Designs
Description: Learn how to creatively manipulate fabric using sustainable techniques such as pleating, gathering, tucking, and other methods that minimize waste and increase longevity. Perfect for costumers and designers looking to reduce their environmental impact.

Title: From Sportswear to Athleisure Wear
Description: Athletic clothing has evolved from restrictive bloomers to chic, high-tech athleisure. This session examines how sportswear influenced women’s fashion through the 20th century and how athletic function and aesthetic merged into daily wear.

Title: Good Mourning
Description: What did it mean to 'mourn properly'? In this lecture, we will discuss the social expectations, clothing, and customs surrounding mourning practices in the 19th and early 20th centuries — including etiquette, symbolism, and surprising rules that governed the grieving process.

Title: Creating a 1920s Haslam System Dress Pattern
Description: This class will demonstrate how to use the Haslam System to draft a stylish 1920s dress pattern. We’ll explore how to interpret original diagrams, adapt them for modern sizes, and walk through key construction points.
Kit Contents: Haslam foundation draft, tracing paper, pencil, curve ruler
Student Provides: Scissors, tape, ruler, and calculator

Title: Faux Fur Regency Mega-Muff
Description: Make your own oversized Regency muff with faux fur! Learn historical inspiration, construction techniques, and how to personalize with trim. Suitable for all skill levels.
Kit Contents: Faux fur, lining fabric, batting, ribbon
Student Provides: Sewing machine, pins, scissors, thread

Title: Gothic Leather Shoulder Pauldron
Description: In this leathercraft workshop, students will make a gothic-style shoulder pauldron. Learn how to cut, shape, dye, and assemble leather using rivets and simple stitching. Great intro to leather armor techniques.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut leather pieces, rivets, straps, hardware, and handouts
Student Provides: Scissors, gloves, pencil or pen, ruler, optional hole punch

Title: Understanding Your Serger
Description: This workshop helps you get comfortable with your serger. Learn threading, adjusting tension, and understanding stitch functions. Bring your own serger or use a classroom machine if available.
Student Provides: Serger, manual, fabric scraps, thread, scissors

Title: Make Your Own Pleater Board
Description: Create your own pleater board, a tool for making even pleats by folding paper or fabric over a guide. This workshop teaches you how to measure, mark, fold, and glue your own customized pleating tool.
Kit Contents: Printed folding templates, foam core backing, glue, clips
Student Provides: Ruler, craft knife, cutting mat

Title: What a Waste: Cross Stitch with Waste Canvas
Description: Learn how to use waste canvas to add cross-stitched embellishments to non-evenweave fabrics like denim or cotton. Great for adding motifs to modern or historical garments.
Kit Contents: Waste canvas, needle, thread, printed motif handouts
Student Provides: Garment or fabric swatch to embroider, small embroidery scissors

Title: All Leather Crossbody Carryall
Description: Construct your own small crossbody bag entirely from leather! Students will learn basic hand-stitching and finishing techniques for leathercraft. No machine required.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut leather panels, strap, hardware, thread, needle, and pattern
Student Provides: Scissors, gloves, ruler, pencil or pen, optional hole punch

Title: Fair Isle: Learn How Easy Colorwork Can Be
Description: An introduction to the Fair Isle knitting technique. Students will learn how to read colorwork charts, manage two yarns, and create their own small sample piece using stranded colorwork.
Kit Contents: Printed colorwork patterns and instruction sheets
Student Provides: Two colors of worsted weight yarn, circular or double-pointed needles (size 6–8), scissors, stitch markers

Title: Reading and Using Big 4 Patterns
Description: This lecture explains how to choose, interpret, and customize commercial patterns from major companies like Simplicity, McCall's, Vogue, and Butterick. We’ll cover terminology, symbols, and modification tips.
Kit Contents: Pattern guides and handouts
Student Provides: Optional: bring a commercial pattern you’ve been struggling to understand

Title: Counted Cross Stitch for Beginners
Description: A gentle introduction to counted cross stitch. You’ll learn to read charts, start a project, manage your threads, and troubleshoot common mistakes. Take home a mini sampler!
Kit Contents: Needle, fabric, hoop, thread, printed sampler chart
Student Provides: Small scissors or snips, optional magnifier

Title: Make a Wire Cage Bustle #1
Description: Build the base of a Victorian-era wire cage bustle. This is part one of a two-part workshop where students will learn to shape, attach, and reinforce the cage structure.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut wire, hoop connectors, tape, instructions
Student Provides: Needle-nose pliers, heavy-duty wire cutters, gloves

Title: Tailoring Basics: An Overview
Description: An introductory overview of tailoring techniques including pad stitching, canvasing, shaping, and traditional inner structure methods used in both menswear and historical garments.

Title: Basic Sewing Terminology
Description: New to sewing or confused by all the jargon? This lecture covers foundational sewing terms, techniques, and tools to help new sewists understand patterns and instructions more easily.

Title: Thanks, It Has Pockets
Description: This class explores the history and politics of pockets in women’s fashion, tracing how pockets evolved from essential to ornamental (or nonexistent) — and what that says about power, practicality, and social norms.

Title: Alterations: Pants and Skirts
Description: Learn common alteration techniques for achieving a great fit in pants and skirts. Topics include adjusting waistbands, hips, and hemlines with both machine and hand techniques.

Title: Details of Extant 18th C Fashion Items
Description: This visual lecture will examine surviving 18th-century garments and accessories up close, focusing on stitching techniques, interior finishing, and period construction choices.

Title: Use and Application of Feathers
Description: Learn how to select, prep, and apply feathers to hats, accessories, and garments for historical or fantasy costuming. We'll cover shaping, curling, wiring, and gluing techniques.
Kit Contents: Feather samples, handout
Student Provides: Notebook, optional gloves

Title: So You Want to Design Your Own Costumes
Description: This lecture covers the basics of costume design for stage and personal projects. Learn about silhouette, character design, mood boards, and practical constraints like movement and construction.

Title: Make a Wire Cage Bustle #2
Description: In this continuation of the morning session, students will complete the cage bustle and learn how to fit and reinforce it for durability and wearability.
Kit Contents: Hoop wire, fabric cover, waistband, connectors
Student Provides: Wire cutters, sewing kit, gloves

Title: Butterfly Hennin: Experimental Archaeology
Description: Recreate a butterfly hennin (the dramatic 15th-century hat) based on historical sources and construction logic. This hands-on session explores speculative historical design using modern materials.
Kit Contents: Base pattern, wire frame, buckram, tulle, and instructions
Student Provides: Sewing kit, scissors, hot glue gun

Title: I Can Hold That: Small Leather Belt Pouch
Description: Construct a functional small leather belt pouch using basic leathercraft tools. Learn cutting, stitching, and finishing techniques while creating a wearable piece.
Kit Contents: Pre-cut leather pieces, thread, button/stud closure, belt loop parts
Student Provides: Scissors, gloves, hole punch (optional)

Title: Fascination
Description: In this class, students will make a fascinator — a small decorative hat or hairpiece — using millinery techniques suitable for both historical and modern costuming. You’ll learn the basics of shaping a base, applying trims, and attaching it securely.
Kit Contents: Base materials, wire, ribbon, comb or clip, and floral trim
Student Provides: Hot glue gun, scissors, optional extra embellishments

Title: Alternative Drafting: Learning from History
Description: Explore how historic and folk garments were drafted and shaped using simple geometry, cultural tradition, and body measurement — long before modern flat patterning. We’ll look at patterning approaches from diverse regions and how to adapt them today.

Title: Care and Keeping of Hats and Hat Boxes
Description: Whether vintage, costume, or millinery pieces, your hats need proper storage and care. Learn how to make your own custom hat boxes and protect delicate embellishments.
Kit Contents: Handouts and sample materials
Student Provides: Optional: photos of your own hat storage issues for Q&A

Title: Alterations: Bodices, Sleeves, and Shoulders
Description: Learn how to adjust bodices and sleeve patterns for better fit at the shoulders, bust, and upper back. Includes how to identify fit issues and where to slash/spread or taper.

Title: Making Your Own Cross Stitch Patterns
Description: Learn how to convert images or motifs into your own counted cross stitch patterns, including best practices for scaling, color selection, and layout. Perfect for costume embroidery or gifts.
Kit Contents: Graph paper, ruler, color key sheet, sample patterns
Student Provides: Pencil, eraser, optional computer/tablet with grid app

Title: Vintage Sewing Machine Attachments
Description: From rufflers to binding feet, vintage sewing machine attachments are clever little tools. This class demos common and unusual attachments, how to use them, and where to find them.

Title: Machine Embroidery with Inkstitch
Description: Join Jen as we dive into the wonderful world of Machine Embroidery with Inkstitch. Inkstitch is a free program you can use to digitize your own embroidery designs. During this lecture, we will walk through the basics of how to create a vector file and transform it into stitches for your embroidery machine.

Title: Laura Ashley & English Country Cottage Design
Description: A designer deepdive on Laura Ashley — her life, historical inspirations, and how she adapted Victorian and Edwardian elements for modern fashion from the 60s–80s. The session includes her ties to Princess Diana and work at the Women’s Institute.

Title: Knitting Techniques for the Sewist
Description: This class will help experienced sewists understand garment shaping in knitting. Learn to relate sewing fit knowledge to vertical darts, short rows, waist and shoulder shaping, and more.

Title: Learn to Dress Yourself in a Japanese Yukata!
Description: Learn the basic dressing techniques for wearing a Yukata (casual cotton kimono). A rental outfit is included, and students can bring their own. We’ll cover dressing steps, accessories, and purchasing options.
Kit Contents: Yukata and accessories for use during class
Student Provides: OPTIONAL: Bring your own yukata, hanhaba obi, koshihimo x2, or other kimono dressing materials

Title: Hand Sewing Basics
Description: Create a sampler of basic hand stitches and fastenings. Students will learn 4 essential hand stitches and 4 fastening techniques commonly used in historical and modern garment construction.
Kit Contents: Sampler blank, instructions, fastenings, needle, and thread
Student Provides: Thread snips, seam ripper, and pins

Title: Paper Piecing Pouches
Description: Create a small pouch using paper piecing, a precise patchwork technique. This hands-on workshop will guide you through layout, stitching, and assembly of a quilted pouch.
Kit Contents: Fabric scraps, paper templates, thread, and printed instructions
Student Provides: Basic sewing kit, scissors, pins, and hand sewing needle

Title: Serging Beyond the Basics
Description: Take your serging skills to the next level. This class will explore rolled hems, differential feed, flatlocking, and decorative threads. Learn how to adjust tension and settings for different effects.
Kit Contents: Handouts, practice fabrics, specialty threads
Student Provides: Serger, instruction manual, basic tools, and coordinating threads

Title: Get Up Close and Personal With 18th C Fashion Items
Description: Examine real 18th-century fashion items in detail. Learn about stitching techniques, fabric choices, and finishing methods by observing and handling museum-quality pieces.

Title: Waraji Straw Sandals
Description: Make your own traditional Japanese waraji sandals using straw or modern fibers. Learn the history and cultural significance of this footwear style and how to weave and tie them.
Kit Contents: Straw/cord, needle, template, and handout
Student Provides: Scissors, tape, and optional mat for working

Title: Fascination
Description: Make a fascinator-style hair ornament using basic millinery techniques. Choose from a variety of trims and base shapes to create your own unique design.
Kit Contents: Base, netting, embellishments, and hand-sewing supplies
Student Provides: Scissors, needle, optional glue gun and custom trims

Title: From Amazon Costume to Historical Clothing
Description: Explore how a costume created for Amazon Prime’s *Wheel of Time* was adapted into a historically inspired ensemble. Includes breakdown of construction changes, fabric sourcing, and adapting fantasy into real-world wear.

Title: Goldwork Embroidery in the Regency Era
Description: Discover the opulent art of goldwork embroidery, a technique used in Regency and earlier periods to embellish garments with metal threads. Class includes visual examples and technique demonstration.

Title: Making a Hatbox
Description: Make your own collapsible hat box to safely store or transport historical hats. This hands-on workshop includes materials for one mid-sized hat box and decorating tips.
Kit Contents: Box templates, cardboard, decorative paper, glue, ribbon
Student Provides: Scissors, hot glue gun, optional decorative items

Title: Heirloom Sewing for the Sewing Machine
Description: Learn to use machine techniques to mimic traditional heirloom sewing. Includes pin tucks, lace insertion, and embellishments typically used in baby garments and historical lingerie.
Kit Contents: Handouts, lace trim, fabric samples, needles
Student Provides: Sewing machine, white thread, scissors

Title: Costuming a Whole Show
Description: Learn the process of costuming a full theatrical production from auditions to curtain call. Topics include budgeting, scheduling, pulling vs. building, cast coordination, and working with directors.

Title: Intro to Natural Dyeing
Description: Learn the basics of dyeing fabric and fiber with natural materials. This workshop will cover common dye plants, mordants, colorfastness, and safety. Students will prepare and dye swatches using beginner-friendly techniques.
Kit Contents: Fabric swatches, sample mordants, dye materials, and handouts
Student Provides: Gloves, apron, and notebook

Title: Victorian Men Were Fashionable, Too
Description: Victorian fashion wasn’t just for women — men were just as image-conscious. This lecture explores the fashion trends, tailoring, and grooming of 19th-century men across classes and cultures.

Title: Cloning Clothes: Patterning from an Extant Garment
Description: Learn how to copy an existing garment without taking it apart. This workshop walks through measuring, marking, and drafting from finished pieces to create usable sewing patterns.
Kit Contents: Dot paper, rulers, pins, and tracing materials
Student Provides: Garment to clone, pencil, measuring tape, and optional French curve

Title: Fantastic Feathers for Hat, Hair, or Clothing
Description: Learn how to use feathers to create headpieces, hat trims, or clothing accents. Covers feather selection, shaping, coloring, and mounting methods with plenty of hands-on work.
Kit Contents: Assorted feathers, wire, glue, clips, embellishment samples
Student Provides: Glue gun, scissors, and optional decorative materials

Title: Intermediate Ribbon Millinery Flowers - Level 2
Description: Take your ribbon flower skills to the next level with advanced petal shaping and floral arrangement. Great for hat embellishment or accessories.
Kit Contents: Precut ribbon, flower centers, floral wire, and instructions
Student Provides: Sewing kit, magnifier optional, scissors

Title: As Seen on TV: Knitwear
Description: A look at how TV shows depict knitwear — both the hits and misses — with attention to historical accuracy, fiber choice, construction, and how knitwear is integrated into costumes.

Title: Digitizing Cutting Files with InkScape
Description: Learn how to turn your design drawings or patterns into digital cut files using Inkscape. Great for use with Cricut or Silhouette cutters for appliqué, vinyl, or stenciling.

Title: How to Teach at Costume College
Description: Curious about being an instructor at Costume College? This session demystifies the process — from application tips to structuring a strong class — and includes a Q&A.

Title: Jeanne Lanvin and the Robe de Style
Description: Explore the signature design of Jeanne Lanvin — the robe de style. Learn what sets it apart from the flapper dress, how it evolved, and how to recreate it authentically.

Title: Warriors of the Steppe: Clothing of the Scythians
Description: Discover the layered, practical, and surprisingly decorative garments of the ancient Scythians, a nomadic people of the Central Asian steppes. This lecture explores archaeology, textile findings, and how to reconstruct their look today.
